title: Near-zero baseline defect rate shift (+0.12 pp vs misleading +600%)
what: Line-C defect rate moves from 0.02% to 0.14% (+0.12 pp absolute change)

reader_questions.question: What is the primary quantitative finding or value?
reader_questions.expected: Line-C defect rate rose from 0.02% to 0.14% (+0.12 pp, +60 defects per 50,000 units).

reader_questions.question: Is the difference clearly outside uncertainty or noise?
reader_questions.expected: Yes; with 50,000 units per period, 10 vs 70 defects is a real jump on Line-C, though absolute yield stays at 99.86%.

reader_questions.question: What caveat, outlier, control, or subgroup pattern matters?
reader_questions.expected: The alarming '+600%' figure is an artifact of dividing by a tiny 0.02% baseline; Lines A, B, and D stayed flat near 0.03–0.04%.
